text:
maya: Heads-up: Veridian on dedicated pool 'dedic-west-3' just reported sustained TPS SLO violations during their marketing blast. Clients seeing admission rejects + intermittent auth errors.

alex: Can you paste the logs you're seeing?

maya: ```
2026-03-15T18:42:12Z admission-controller pool=dedic-west-3 tps=5120 window=60s burst_credits=0 action=reject reason=burst_credit_exhausted
2026-03-15T18:42:13Z proxy     pool=dedic-west-3 upstream=runtime-7 host=10.4.3.21 resp=429 path=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T18:42:15Z auth      user=veridian svc=token-refresh status=401 err="token expired"
```

ops-bot: ALERT: admission-controller pool=dedic-west-3 breached TPS SLO (target=4k, observed=5.1k, duration=00:00:45)

kevin: Are they on prewarm? What's reserved capacity look like for that pool right now?

maya: They have reserved 10 GPUs (reserved_capacity=10), current_util=92%, queued_requests=117. Burst credits dropped to 0 within ~90s of the spike. Billing pipeline shows a lag; charges didn't reflect the spike yet.

sara: Repro steps I used locally to emulate:
```bash
# 500 concurrent short requests + 50 long-context ones
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}' & done
for j in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"long...","max_tokens":8192}' & done
wait
```
That pattern reproduces quick burst + heavy long-context noise that drains KV cache and burst credits.

kevin: We also saw a noisy neighbor: tenant 'PulseAI' launched several 32k-context jobs around the same time. KV cache hit rate fell from 0.88 -> 0.22 and host GPU mem pressure spiked, which slowed preemption and increased latencies.

maya: Auth errors look like token refresh storms: many clients keep retrying when they get 429 which amplifies the load. Also saw a few 502s from runtime timeouts when queueing lengthened.

oncall-ryan: Immediate mitigation plan (3 steps):
1) Apply temporary rate-limit override to PulseAI (rlimit set to 1000 tps) to stop noisy neighbor.
2) Increase admission headroom for dedic-west-3 from 20% -> 35% to give breathing room for preemption/fallback.
3) Trigger manual top-up of Veridian's burst credits and open billing ticket for accelerated accounting.

oncall-ryan: Commands:```
# throttle tenant
redwoodctl tenants update --id pulseai --qos "burst=1000" --comment "temp noisy neighbor throttle"
# bump admission headroom
redwoodctl pool update --name dedic-west-3 --admission-headroom 0.35
# top-up burst credits (admin)
redwoodctl billing topup --account veridian --credits 50000 --reason "emergency top-up"
```

billing-bot: Invoice created INV-7832 and auto-topup queued; expected propagation to charging system ~2m.

alex: Medium-term: we should add a guardrail that routes very long-context jobs (>32k) to best-effort pools by default, and enforce per-tenant long-job concurrency limits so single tenants can't evict headroom.

maya: Also proposing these runtime changes for stability: 1) admission smoothing (token-bucket smoothing window=10s), 2) preemptive fallback to smaller model variants when burst_credits<=50, 3) reduce KV cache TTL for tail requests to 10s to avoid large-context cache churn. I'll patch the admission-controller and roll to canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for admission-controller on dedic-west-3 (canary hosts 1/3).

oncall-ryan: If the patch doesn't arrest the breach within 5m, we escalate to infra to add additional prewarmed hosts or shift some reserved capacity temporarily. Also add SDK guidance to clients: exponential backoff + jitter on 429, and recommend smaller-context fallbacks.

maya: I'll coordinate with billing + support to confirm Veridian's top-up and send customer-facing mitigation instructions (recommend routing traffic into two pools and enabling fallback model). Will update thread with post-mortem notes.

alex: Thanks — keep me posted. If this recurs, we'll formalize a headroom playbook and a permanent QoS tag for long-context jobs.
